chapter_name: Stem Cell Culture and Organ Culture
learning_objective: 🧬 Understand the 'master cells' of the body and the futuristic science of growing 3D tissues and organs in the lab!

key_vocabulary.hindi_meaning: मूल कोशिका (ऐसी कोशिका जो शरीर की किसी भी अन्य कोशिका में बदल सकती है)
बहुशक्त (लगभग सभी प्रकार के ऊतकों में विकसित होने की क्षमता)

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Stem cells have two unique properties: self-renewal (they can divide and make more of themselves indefinitely) and potency (they can differentiate into specialized cells like heart, nerve, or skin cells).

Embryonic Stem Cells (ESCs) are pluripotent (can become any cell in the body) but raise ethical issues since they come from embryos. Adult Stem Cells (like in bone marrow) are multipotent (can only become a limited number of cell types).

A breakthrough! Scientists found a way to take a normal adult skin cell and reprogram it genetically to act exactly like an Embryonic Stem Cell. This bypasses ethical issues and avoids immune rejection since the cells are from the patient.

Combining cells, engineering, and materials to improve or replace biological tissues. It involves a 'scaffold' (a 3D framework), 'cells' (usually stem cells), and 'growth factors' to tell the cells what to do.

Using 3D printing technology, but instead of plastic, the printer uses 'bio-ink' (living cells and gel) to print layers of tissue, moving us closer to the dream of printing whole organs for transplantation.

fun_activity.title: 🧠 Mini-Brains in a Dish
fun_activity.instructions: Scientists are currently using stem cells to grow 'cerebral organoids'—tiny, pea-sized, 3D models of human brains. While they can't think, they fire electrical signals and are used to study diseases like Alzheimer's and the Zika virus without experimenting on humans!

exam_tips: 📌 Clearly define the hierarchy of potency: Totipotent (can form a whole organism + placenta) > Pluripotent (all body cells) > Multipotent (specific family of cells, like blood cells).
📌 iPSCs (Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells) are highly testable. Mention Shinya Yamanaka, who won the Nobel Prize for this discovery.
📌 Explain that tissue engineering relies heavily on 'scaffolds' made of biocompatible materials to give cells a 3D structure to grow on.
quick_recap: ⭐ Bone marrow transplantation for leukemia is the most widely established clinical use of adult stem cells.
⭐ Organ culture involves growing whole organs or parts of organs in vitro while maintaining their structural and functional integrity.
⭐ The umbilical cord blood is a rich and non-controversial source of hematopoietic stem cells.
